newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian nuclear arms systems decaying - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russian nuclear arms systems decaying - minister.

text.p: Defence Minister Igor Rodionov said on Thursday Russia's armed forces had deteriorated so much that the reliablity of its nuclear weapons systems was in question, Interfax news agency said.

Rodionov, stepping up calls for military reforms, was quoted by Interfax as telling senior representatives of the Russian media: "Russia might soon reach the threshold beyond which its rockets and nuclear systems cannot be controlled."
Rodionov, 60, said he had outlined his concerns about the decline in the armed forces in a letter addressed to President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Interfax quoted Rodionov as saying Russia's combat readiness had been dropping constantly since 1990 and its weapons systems were falling into decay while the United States, Moscow's former Cold War foe, was improving its own systems.

Rodionov also said he was alarmed by the psychological frame of mind of many troops, especially officers. The number of suicides in the military, once minimal, had risen to about 100 in 1996, he said.

His comments were the latest shots in a battle he has been waging over reforms since he was appointed by Yeltsin last July. "The whole horror is in the fact that, as Russian defence minister, I am becoming a spectator of the destructive processes in the army and can nothing about it, " he said.
